So we have all seen posts about spying, read pastebins of the 100 or so networks and sites that MS feeds your data into while ignoring your host files, but can it be stopped using a good external hardware firewall? I have a router that I have plugged nearly 100 addresses into, but would a good hardware firewall that we could add all of these into work better? I have switched to Linux Mint already for my laptop where I do all my personal stuff, so I have a HTPC and a gaming PC left with windows 10 on them. I will move the HTPC eventually to Linux but in the meantime would it be worth investing in a good firewall?

Yes, a firewall can drop that traffic, just like your consumer router can. Are you experiencing any bandwidth degradation with your current setup?

If the router you've already got is doing the job, then another network appliance would likely be a waste.

Don't get me wrong. I think more folks should have a pfSense box running their home network, but it certainly isn't for everyone, and an improperly configured router/firewall is likely to do more harm than good.

I don't think I'm experiencing bandwidth degradation. All I did was copy/paste about 100 sites into my router's block section. Would a pfSense box eliminate the risk of bandwidth degradation vs say my consumer router? I don't think I will worry about it since I don't seem to be experiencing any issues but I appreciate the input.

I'd at least paste some of those domains into a browser to make sure they're being blocked. I'd also run some speed tests to verify your bandwidth. If everything looks good, then I wouldn't worry about buying extra stuff.

pfSense is network appliance OS, and its capabilities are largely determined by the hardware you install it on. That said, you might be surprised at how much you can do with a relatively inexpensive Atom box.
